items.body: Single biggest injury cause for travelers: jumping back to full mileage too fast. Resume at the planned week's volume, not the missed week's volume.
1-2 weeks of REDUCED running (even half mileage) loses minimal aerobic fitness. Tissue adaptation slows but doesn't reverse. The plan absorbs this.
Have a Good / Realistic / Minimal version so you can adapt based on how the trip actually unfolds. Land at Minimal? Fine. Don't catastrophize.
Wk 3 (Jun 29-Jul 5): partial — at home Mon-Thu, travel Thu night, in Italy Fri-Sun. Wk 4 (Jul 6-12): all in Italy.
No gym — bodyweight only. Push-ups, pull-ups (find a bar/doorway), squats, lunges, plank, glute bridges. 20-30 min, 3-4x during the trip.
25-28 mi (vs original 30). Get Mon-Thu morning runs done at home as planned. Sat long run in Italy at 8-10 mi (shorter than planned 13 — jetlag, exploring).

travel.heading: Wk 4 — pick the scenario that fits your trip

items.body: 22-26 mi. 4 runs of 5-6 mi + 1 longer 8-10 mi. Treat as a cutback week.
15-20 mi. 3 runs of 4-6 mi + 1 medium 7-8 mi. Still a real cutback. EXPECTED DEFAULT.
8-12 mi. 2-3 short runs of 3-5 mi only. Bodyweight on other days. Walk a lot.

Resume planned 31 mi. Don't try to make up Italy. Easy days the first 3-4 days back will feel harder due to jetlag — HR will be higher at same pace, so pace will be slower. That's correct, not a problem.
Hot in July. Run early morning (cooler + before tourist crowds). Hydration discipline — easy to under-drink on vacation. Practice gel + water on long run if you can carry it.
Original plan had Wk 10 as the SHARPEST hill week (37 mi, peak hill repeats). That can't happen during a wedding trip. The Wk 9-10-11 block has been redesigned in the main plan.
Old: Wk 9 cutback (29) → Wk 10 peak hills (37) → Wk 11 build (38). New: Wk 9 peak hills (37) → Wk 10 travel cutback (15-25) → Wk 11 conservative bounce (33).

items.term: Wk 9 — DO HARD WORK BEFORE TRIP
items.body: Move the peak hill workout to Wednesday and the long run to Thursday so they're done before you fly Friday Aug 14. If you can only manage one before leaving, prioritize the LONG RUN over the hill workout (long run is harder to replace on the road).
Mon Legs / Tue 6 + Chest-Tri / WED HILL REPEATS / THU 14-mile long run / Fri travel + Sh-Arms or skip / Sat-Sun rest or short shakeouts at the trip.
Hotel gym available. Do Chest/Tri and Back/Bi if energy allows. SKIP LEGS this week — they need rest from Wk 9's hill work anyway.
20-25 mi. 3 hotel treadmill runs of 4-5 mi + 1 outdoor 8-10 mi. 2 hotel gym lifts (upper-body only).
12-18 mi. 2-3 short runs of 4-5 mi + 1 medium 6-8 mi. 1-2 upper-body lifts. EXPECTED DEFAULT.
6-10 mi. 2 short hotel treadmill runs. Walk a lot. 0-1 lifts.
Don't even try to run the wedding day itself or the day after if it's a late night. Sleep matters more than mileage.
Reduced from original 38 mi to 33 mi. Long run drops from 16 to 12 mi. Threshold workout shortened from 3 x 1 mi to 2 x 1 mi. Don't snap back to full volume.
Resume original plan at 40 mi. The August trip costs ~15 miles total across Wks 10-11. That's a fair price; the plan absorbs it.
Shoes, 3-4 pairs running socks, 2-3 lightweight running shirts/shorts, watch + charger, gels (TSA OK), SaltStick caps, body glide. Hat optional but helpful.
Treadmill is fine for easy mileage. Set 1% incline to roughly approximate outdoor effort. Don't try hard workouts on treadmills in hotel gyms — they're often low quality and uneven.

Run early morning when traveling east (your body still thinks it's earlier — easier to wake up). Hydrate aggressively the first 2-3 days; jetlag dehydrates. Don't try to PR a workout in the first 4-5 days.

3 rounds of: 15 push-ups, 15 bodyweight squats, 10 lunges/leg, 30s plank, 12 glute bridges. Optional: pull-ups if a bar is available. Maintains movement patterns; doesn't replace your lifts but keeps you out of the hole.
If you're getting <5 hours sleep, traveling all day, or hungover from wedding — REST. A skipped run on poor sleep is better than a run that wrecks tomorrow.
Calf/achilles tightness in mile 1-2 that fades = normal. Pain that gets WORSE during a run, or any sharp pain = stop. Don't 'push through' on vacation when medical access is unfamiliar.
If easy pace HR is 10+ bpm higher than normal for 3+ days after returning, you came back too fast or are sick. Drop another week to easy-only.
If the foot numbness you mentioned earlier escalates during travel (different shoes, more walking, etc.), don't ignore it. Note when it happens and address back home.
60-75 g/hour. For a 3:45 marathon, aim for ~70 g/hr.
400-500 mg/hour. THIS IS YOUR CRAMP LEVER — currently likely <100 mg/hr.
16-24 oz/hr (about 4-6 oz every 15-20 min). Start sipping at mile 2-3, NOT when thirsty.
Optional. If used: 100-200 mg total, not per hour. Use mostly for race day or peak workouts.
~22g carb, ~25 mg sodium, dual-source. 3/hr = 66g carb, 75 mg sodium.
~24g carb, ~250 mg sodium, ~25 mg caffeine. 3/hr = 72g carb, 750 mg sodium (TOO MUCH if also using salt caps).
30g carb per gel, dual-source. Top marathon gel. ~3/hr easily hits 90g if you want it. Try ONE on a long run before committing.
40g carb per gel — highest mainstream. Thick, sweet, divisive. Only if you want to push to 80-120g/hr.
25g carb, hydrogel, gentlest on gut. Pricey. Good if any GI issues develop.
Don't switch yet. Huma works. Fix sodium and water first. If switching later, try Precision PF 30 as natural step up.
Your 60-min cramp pattern fits sodium depletion timeline. Current likely intake ~75 mg/hr (3 Huma standard); target is 300-600 mg/hr.
215 mg sodium per capsule, take with water every 30-45 min. Easy to carry. RECOMMENDED START.
1000 mg sodium per stick pack, mix in 16-32 oz water. One pack = full hour's sodium. Good if using handheld/flask.
250-500 mg sodium per cap depending on version. Pricier alternative to SaltStick.
Standard Huma gels x 3/hr + SaltStick Caps x 2/hr + 16-20 oz plain water/hr. = 66g carb, 75+430=505 mg sodium/hr. Hits all targets.
Huma Plus gels x 3/hr (each has electrolytes) + plain water. = 72g carb, 750 mg sodium/hr. Sodium runs high but acceptable if you're a heavy sweater.
Standard Huma x 3/hr + LMNT stick in 20 oz water/hr. = 66g carb, 1075 mg sodium/hr. Sodium too high unless heavy sweater in heat. Use HALF an LMNT pack instead = ~575 mg.
Start with Option A. Use Plus gels only on hardest long runs / race day for caffeine boost (max 2 Plus per long run, rest standard).
You haven't been drinking on runs. Highest-impact fix in your nutrition picture.
16-24 oz/hr. Sip every 15-20 min. Start drinking at mile 2-3, not when thirsty (thirst lags ~30 min).
Optional. Drink based on thirst.

HANDHELD BOTTLE (Nathan/Salomon, 12-20 oz): simplest, fine up to ~12 mi. HYDRATION VEST (Salomon ADV Skin 5, Nathan Pinnacle 4L): needed for 15+ mi solo runs. NYC race day has aid stations every mile — no vest needed for race.
~110-130 oz/day (~half body weight in oz, more on running days). Pee color check: pale yellow = good, dark = drink more.
Your gut needs adaptation to absorb 60-75g carb/hr. Untrained gut = bonk or GI distress at race. Build it up gradually in long runs.
Wk 1-3: water + 1 gel on long run. Wk 4-6: water + 2 gels + 1 SaltStick. Wk 7-10: water + 3 gels + 2 SaltStick. Wk 11+: full race fueling (3-4 gels/hr + sodium).
Long-run cells now include fueling cues for each week's practice level.
780-940 g carbs/day for 1-2 days before race (about 10-12 g/kg). Feels uncomfortable; that's the point. Bagels, pasta, rice, white bread, sports drinks.
~160g carbs (bagel + banana + sports drink). Last bathroom break ~30 min before start.
One gel (caffeinated optional). 6-8 oz water.
1 gel (24 g) every 2.5 mi → ~10 total, ≈ 60–67 g/hr. SaltStick every 30–45 min (~6 total). Water 4–6 oz every 15–20 min at aid stations. (Matches the Fueling panel + Race card in the app.)
Total ~250-350 mg. Coffee morning of (~100mg) + 1-2 caffeinated gels late race (Huma Plus or similar). Don't stack too high — GI risk.
Do a sweat test this summer (weigh before/after a 60-min run, account for fluid drunk). Tells you ACTUAL sweat rate and informs sodium per hour. Worth doing twice (cool day, hot day).
Test every nutrition variable in TRAINING before race day. Never try new gel/drink/cap for the first time on Nov 1.

paces.heading: SUB-3:45 NYC MARATHON — KEY, PACES & RATIONALE

Now 44 mi (was 46). Matches example PDF's peak.
Added to long-run cells throughout. Builds gut training week by week.
~75-80% easy. Slightly more conservative than tester's 65-75% because tissue is the limiter.
Tue/Wed/Thu AM. Thursday = weekly QUALITY session.

Legs (Mon) / Chest-Tri (Tue) / Back-Bi (Thu — but no lift Thu in higher weeks) / Sh-Arms (Fri). 4-day.
